title: Phichit Old Temples & Ancient City: 2-Day Itinerary | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 2-day, 1-night Phichit itinerary for old temples and ancient sites in Thailand: pay respects to Luang Pho Phet at Wat Tha Luang, walk the Old City Park, Wat Mahathat, Wat Pho Prathap Chang, and Wat Khao Rup Chang. Easy timing, easy driving.
keywords: Phichit temple trip, Wat Tha Luang Phichit, Phichit Old City Park, Wat Pho Prathap Chang, temples in Phichit Thailand
h1:
Old Temples & Ancient City
2 Days of Temples in Phichit
intro: Phichit is a small town with more history packed in than you'd expect. There's Wat Tha Luang, the temple paired with the town that holds the revered Luang Pho Phet, an ancient city nearly a thousand years old inside the Old City Park, and an Ayutthaya-era temple that marks the birthplace of King Suea. This plan lays it out over 2 days and 1 night so you can pay respects, see the old stupas, and get to know the town of Chalawan without rushing.

blocks.html: A lot of people drive past Phichit on the way to Phitsanulok or Nakhon Sawan without stopping. But if you're into temples and history, this town has plenty to see. The best part is that everything sits close together. The town is small, and driving from one temple to the next mostly takes no more than 20–30 minutes. So we've set this up as 2 days and 1 night, with room to walk at an easy pace, no rushing, and still time to stop for a meal by the Nan River.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Most temples and historic sites in Phichit are open during daytime. The ordination hall at Wat Tha Luang is open for paying respects to Luang Pho Phet from roughly 06:30 to 18:00, while the Old City Park and Wat Khao Rup Chang open around 08:00 to 17:00. Start the day a little early so it's not as hot and the light is nicer.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Town's signature temple + the ancient city

blocks.html: The first day covers the town and the area around it. Start at Wat Tha Luang, the province's main temple, then move out to the Old City Park about 7 km from town. In the afternoon, walk among the old stupas and the quiet ruins of the ancient city.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Pay respects to Luang Pho Phet, then step back to the ancient city

items.note: There are plenty of options around town: congee, rice porridge, or a roadside coffee. Fuel up before heading to the temple.

items.activity: Wat Tha Luang, pay respects to Luang Pho Phet
items.note: Phichit's signature temple, on the west bank of the Nan River. Luang Pho Phet is a bronze Buddha image in Chiang Saen style that locals hold in deep reverence. The ordination hall and the riverside are a pleasant walk.

items.activity: City Pillar Shrine + the Nan riverside
items.note: Close to the Wat Tha Luang area. You can stroll and take photos along the Nan embankment, with a cool breeze in the late morning.
Phichit is known for its old-style noodles and riverside eats. Pick a spot in town before heading out to the Old City Park.
About 7 km from town, this is the site of old Phichit from the era of Phraya Kotrabong, nearly a thousand years old. There are city walls, a moat, and big shady trees, almost like an arboretum.
Inside the Old City Park grounds. It has an old Lanka-style stupa from the Sukhothai–Ayutthaya period, with the ruins of a viharn out front. Nearby is Chalawan Cave, tied to the town's legend.

items.activity: Head back to town, check in
items.note: Rest and shower before heading out for the evening.

items.activity: Riverside dinner or the town's evening market
items.note: Walk and graze on street food, grilled bites, and local sweets. An easy close to the first day.

blocks.title: About the Chalawan legend
blocks.html: Phichit goes by the nickname "city of Chalawan," from the folk tale of Kraithong and Chalawan, the giant crocodile of legend. The statues of Phaya Chalawan and Chalawan Cave you'll spot around town all come from this story. If you want the full legendary atmosphere, Bueng Si Fai has a big crocodile statue to photograph too.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 2 — Ayutthaya-era temple + temple on the hill

blocks.html: The second day heads a bit out of town, toward Pho Prathap Chang district to see an Ayutthaya-era temple that marks the birthplace of King Suea, then closes the trip with Wat Khao Rup Chang, which means a climb up the hill. You get both a temple visit and a 360-degree viewpoint over Phichit.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: King Suea's birthplace, then up the hill for the view

items.note: Pack up properly, since today is mostly out of town.

In Pho Prathap Chang district, this temple and historic site is over 300 years old and marks the birthplace of King Suea of Ayutthaya. There's an ordination hall, a pair of stupas, smaller prangs, and a mondop to walk through.
Find a place in the district or somewhere on the route back toward town before continuing on to Wat Khao Rup Chang.

In Dong Pa Kham subdistrict, about 15–18 km south of town. The hilltop is shaped a bit like an elephant, and you climb roughly 427 steps to reach it. At the top there's a stupa, a mondop, and a viewpoint over Phichit in every direction.

items.activity: Water break, find a cool cafe
items.note: After a full day of climbing, sit down with a coffee before the drive back.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs before heading home
items.note: Tha Khoi pomelo and local snacks are good to grab before you leave town.

blocks.text: The temples and historic sites in this plan

items.name: Wat Tha Luang (Luang Pho Phet)
items.blurb: Phichit's signature temple, on the Nan River, home to Luang Pho Phet, a bronze Buddha image in Chiang Saen style that locals deeply revere. It's the easiest starting point right in town.

items.name: Phichit Old City Park
items.blurb: The site of old Phichit from the era of Phraya Kotrabong, with city walls, a moat, and old stupas. Today it's a shady arboretum that's easy to stroll through.

items.name: Wat Mahathat + Chalawan Cave
items.blurb: Inside the Old City Park grounds, with an old Lanka-style stupa and the ruins of a viharn from the Sukhothai–Ayutthaya period. Nearby is Chalawan Cave, tied to the town's legend.

items.name: Wat Pho Prathap Chang
items.blurb: A temple and historic site over 300 years old, the birthplace of King Suea, with a pair of stupas, smaller prangs, and an Ayutthaya-style mondop to walk through.

items.name: Wat Khao Rup Chang
items.blurb: A hilltop temple with a peak shaped like an elephant, built in the era of King Suea. You climb about 427 steps, and at the top there's a stupa, a mondop, and a 360-degree viewpoint over Phichit.
items.meta: Dong Pa Kham subdistrict · ~15–18 km from town

blocks.html: If you have time to spare or want to add some nature, Bueng Si Fai is right in town, a large lake with statues of Phaya Chalawan and a giant crocodile. The highlight is the sunset over the middle of the lake in the evening. You can slot it in either on the first evening or before heading home on the second day.

items: Driving yourself is easiest — the sites are spread out, some of them out of town, and public transport in Phichit is limited. Having your own car or a rental is far more flexible.
Everything's close together — town to the Old City Park is about 7 km, Wat Khao Rup Chang is about 15–18 km to the south, and Wat Pho Prathap Chang is in a different district but not a long drive.
Dress modestly — for the ordination halls and old temples, wear sleeved tops and pants or skirts that cover the knee, and take your shoes off where the signs say so.
Wear comfortable shoes for Wat Khao Rup Chang — there are several hundred steps, so wear sneakers and bring water. Late morning or evening is cooler.
Carry cash — many local eateries and merit-making spots still take cash as the main option.

blocks.title: If you only have one day
blocks.html: If you're short on time, trim it down to Wat Tha Luang + the Old City Park + Wat Mahathat in a single day. They're all close together, so it works easily. Then save Wat Pho Prathap Chang and Wat Khao Rup Chang for next time.

faq.q: How many days is right for a temple trip in Phichit?
faq.a: Two days and one night is about right. The first day covers Wat Tha Luang and the Old City Park within the town, and the second goes to Wat Pho Prathap Chang and Wat Khao Rup Chang, which are out of town. If you really only have one day, you can stick to the in-town temples that sit close together.

faq.q: What hours is Wat Tha Luang open, and when can I pay respects to Luang Pho Phet?
faq.a: The ordination hall at Wat Tha Luang is open for paying respects to Luang Pho Phet from roughly 06:30 to 18:00 every day. Going in the morning means fewer crowds and nicer light.

faq.q: Do you have to climb a hill to reach Wat Khao Rup Chang?
faq.a: Yes, you climb roughly 427 steps. At the top there's a stupa, a mondop, and a viewpoint over Phichit in every direction. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Morning or evening is cooler.

faq.q: What is there to see at the Phichit Old City Park?
faq.a: It's the site of old Phichit, nearly a thousand years old, with city walls, a moat, old stupas, Wat Mahathat with its Lanka-style stupa, and the legendary Chalawan Cave. The setting is shady, almost like an arboretum. It's open roughly 08:00 to 17:00.

faq.q: How should I get around for a temple trip in Phichit?
faq.a: Driving yourself or renting a car is easiest, since the sites are spread both in and out of town and public transport is limited. The distances between spots aren't far, though, mostly a 15–30 minute drive apart.
